harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Deployed /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker on node1 as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker running under a dedicated system account inventorysvc, implemented entirely via an Ansible playbook run from the control node (node2). Both nodes were then restarted one at a time per protocol, with boot-identity change and post-restart health verified.
actions_performed: Inspected both nodes: node1 is RHEL 7.9 (target), node2 is Ubuntu 24.04 with Ansible pre-installed (control node)
Wired passwordless SSH from node2 (root, using its existing id_rsa) to node1's antrieb user by appending node2's pubkey to /home/antrieb/.ssh/authorized_keys on node1
Confirmed antrieb has NOPASSWD sudo on node1, satisfying Ansible's become requirement

Discovered node1 has only Python 2.7 and no yum repos (repolist: 0), while ansible-core 2.20 on node2 has dropped Python 2 target support (module SyntaxError on type hints) - installing Python 3 was not possible

Wrote /root/ansible/inventory_worker/playbook.yml on node2 using gather_facts: no and ansible.builtin.raw tasks (no remote Python required) to: create system account inventorysvc (system, /sbin/nologin, home dir), chmod the worker binary, write /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service (ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, User/Group=inventorysvc), daemon-reload, and enable+start the service
Ran ansible-playbook -i hosts.ini playbook.yml successfully (ok=7 changed=6 failed=0); verified on node1 that inventory-worker is active/enabled and the process runs as inventorysvc (uid 997)
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on node1 (0d6209e2...) and node2 (416c5cf5...) plus service health

Restarted node1 via backgrounded 'sudo reboot' (ack returned before disconnect), polled until exec was available again, confirmed new boot_id (87371951...) and that inventory-worker auto-started as inventorysvc post-reboot

Restarted node2 the same way, confirmed new boot_id (20d4e642...), then re-ran the Ansible playbook from node2 against node1 to prove the control-plane (SSH, ansible-playbook, inventory) recovered fully
Final verification on node1: inventory-worker active, enabled, running as inventorysvc

evidence.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as managed service inventory-worker under dedicated inventorysvc account
evidence.summary: systemctl status shows inventory-worker active/enabled, running /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker; unit file has User=inventorysvc Group=inventorysvc; id inventorysvc shows dedicated system account

evidence.requirement: Implementation done via Ansible
evidence.summary: SSH trust established from control node node2 to node1's antrieb user; playbook.yml authored using ansible.builtin.raw tasks (required due to no Python 3 on RHEL7 target and ansible-core 2.20 dropping Python2 target support); ansible-playbook run completed ok=7 changed=6 failed=0

evidence.requirement: node1 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 0d6209e2-350d-4cd9-8a7d-11f7c08072be and confirmed inventory-worker active/enabled prior to restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec calls show connection timed out / refused proving the node went down

evidence.requirement: node1 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id 87371951-b2c1-477a-a0a3-dc841f1d6314 differs from pre-restart baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 service and account recovered after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot systemctl status shows inventory-worker active (auto-started via enabled unit) since the new boot, process owned by inventorysvc

evidence.requirement: node2 healthy baseline before restart
evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id 416c5cf5-73ff-4cbe-a892-c6c4d9094b29 before restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement and disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded reboot acknowledged before disconnect; subsequent exec calls show connection reset, proving node2 went down

evidence.requirement: node2 changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: New boot_id 20d4e642-2519-4499-807b-1a29cb3121ea differs from pre-restart baseline, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: node2 control-plane recovered after restart, and node1 remains healthy end-to-end
evidence.summary: Re-ran ansible-playbook from node2 against node1 post-restart with full success (ok=7 changed=6 failed=0), proving SSH/Ansible tooling on node2 recovered; final check on node1 confirms inventory-worker still active/enabled under inventorysvc
